messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm making good headway on implementing a hierarchical version of the Linear Ballistic Accumulator model of human response time and accuracy in simple perceptual discrimination experiments. The code I wrote (https://gist.github.com/mike-lawrence/5860316) seems to pass the first error checks that RStan performs before compiling, but as soon as stan begins sampling I get a crash (in both the R gui and at command line) with the error message:

    R(93016) malloc: *** error for object 0x109acec98: pointer being freed was not allocated
    *** set a breakpoint in malloc_error_break to debug

I've tried compiling and running the resulting binary from the command line, but I get the same error message. 

Any suggestions as to what I should do next to track down what's going awry?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re:
parts:
On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 1:57:44 PM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:
Any suggestions as to what I should do next to track down what's going awry?

It's the last line

lp__ <- lp__ + (log1m(otherResponseCDF)+log(thisResponsePDF));

log1m() requires its argument to be <= 1, which isn't guaranteed to be the case in your model. Actually, I think it is guaranteed to not be the case as written:

otherResponseCDF <- 1+(tmp1+tmp2)/thisStartMax[subject[i]];

If tmp1, tmp2, and thisStartMax[subject[i]] are all positive then otherResponseCDF is always going to greater than 1.

Ben

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re:
parts:
After a lot of playing around, it seems that the culprit is indeed the fact that "otherResponseCDF" is occasionally greater than 1, causing log1m() to throw an error. Actually, it's only ever minutely greater than 1 (ex. 1+1.04361e-14, 1+6.21725e-15, etc), so I suspect this is a precision issue of some sort (I'm only vaguely familiar with the idea that computers can have trouble representing numbers precisely) . Adding the line:

    otherResponseCDF <- if_else(otherResponseCDF>1,1,otherResponseCDF);

solves things.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: CDF values > 1
parts:
Thanks for reporting. I'm cc-ing stan-dev.

Can we change the behavior of the CDFs to
do this internally without changing their derivatives?
That way we can have the best of both worlds.

The problem with the proposed solution

> otherResponseCDF <- if_else(otherResponseCDF>1,1,otherResponseCDF);

is that when the condition is true, you lose the connection
to the derivative. This may not be apparent in a large model,
but it's not the right thing to do.

- Bob
